subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A minus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted upward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '2)'. The MIRROR of rule 1, and I read both halves separately rather than inferring them from rule 1's arm. (1) PRODUCE-THE-CHARACTER. CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 363 'char osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' writes '-' for a negative argument-4/argument-3, with the MAGNITUDE taken through Math.Abs at line 361 so the offset-hours/offset-minutes subfields carry the unsigned value the subformat wants. The negative value survives the emitter intact: IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFormattedTime / #RenderFormattedDatetime pass the offset through ArgInt -> AsInt -> RuntimeApi.IntegerArg, a raising (not wrapping) narrowing to long, not through any absolute-value or unsigned carrier. Verified by golden: conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'OFF-MIN=010000-2359' for FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm" 3600 -1439) -- the format's placeholder is '+' and the DATA carries '-', which is precisely the shape §15.3.3.6.1 describes. (2) HONOUR-THE-MEANING (adjust UPWARD). EmitFormatted line 328 'secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m' with a NEGATIVE offset ADDS, then lines 329-330 roll the day. Verified by golden: conformance:cases/_unassigned/r25_utc_roll_date_range case 3, FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ" 3067670 86399 -1439) -> '99991231T235859Z' -- local 9999-12-30 23:59:59 adjusted UPWARD by 23h59m to 9999-12-31 23:58:59 UTC. This is the direction NOTE 1 of rule 3 illustrates ('0514278124-0500' == '1014278124Z'), and CobolDate.cs#FormattedCurrentDate reproduces exactly that shape for a west-of-UTC system clock (offMin = -300 -> osign '-', oh 05, om 00, with now.TimeOfDay giving the LOCAL common time). (3) CONSUME-THE-CHARACTER. Analyze lines 513-515 accept '-' through the same single expression that accepts '+' ('if (c is not ('+' or '-')) { ... }' -- both signs take the identical no-op branch), and no downstream use is required: §15.79.4 and the §15.48.4 r1 NOTE (both --check OK, see GR-15.3.3.6.1-1) confine the returned values to the common-time / date subfields. HONEST RESIDUE: no golden feeds a '-' sign into a CONSUMING function (pb23 exercises the shared branch with '+' only); that half rests on implementation reading, of a single expression in which '+' and '-' are literally the same arm, so the two-arm-dispatch scar does not apply. Editions rationale identical to GR-15.3.3.6.1-1. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS, but TWO load-bearing claims in the note above are WRONG and the record is changed. (1) TEST-REF CORRECTED: conformance:cases/_unassigned/r25_utc_roll_date_range is REMOVED for the same reason as on GR-15.3.3.6.1-1 -- its format 'YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ' is a §15.3.3.5 UTC format with no offset subformat, so it emits no sign character and cannot be evidence about what a '-' in offset-subformat data MEANS. That leaves pb11's OFF-MIN=010000-2359 as the only test, and it closes only the WRITE-THE-CHARACTER half; unlike rule 1, NO golden anywhere pairs a minus-sign rendering with its UTC equivalent, so the meaning half here rests on reading alone. (2) THE NOTE'S CLAIM THAT THE NEGATIVE VALUE REACHES THE RENDERER 'not through any absolute-value or unsigned carrier' IS FALSE. Math.Abs is applied to it TWICE: CobolDate.cs EmitFormatted line 361 ('long offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes)') and CobolDate.cs OffsetOutOfRange line 446 ('if (!hasOffset || Math.Abs(offsetMinutes) <= 1439) return false'). The second one is unguarded at long.MinValue, where Math.Abs throws OverflowException, and CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg (CobolIntrinsics.cs line 139) ADMITS long.MinValue (v >= long.MinValue is inclusive), so FORMATTED-TIME('hhmmss+hhmm', 3600, W) with W = -9223372036854775808 faults a raw CLR exception out of the intrinsic where §15.3 permits only EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and the default -- the same escaping-CLR-fault shape kb/Work PB23 and R25 each closed once. IT DOES NOT CHANGE THIS VERDICT: I traced the order and the guard runs BEFORE EmitFormatted (FormattedTime line 404-407, FormattedDatetime line 458-462), and when hasOffset is false the renderer passes the literal 0 (IntrinsicRenderer RenderFormattedTime/RenderFormattedDatetime), so line 361 is unreachable with that value and no offset-subformat DATA is at stake. The defect belongs to §15.41.3 r4 / §15.40.3 r5 (rows AR-15.41.3-4, AR-15.40.3-5), not to §15.3.3.6.1, and attributing it here would be the wrong-clause error. (3) THE 'SAME offsetMinutes DRIVES BOTH' ARGUMENT IS WEAKER THAN STATED and I re-derived it rather than inheriting it: EmitFormatted line 328 runs only when isUtc, and the osign write at line 363/382 runs only when an OffSign segment exists, which a 'Z' format never has -- the two branches are DISJOINT and never co-execute, so they share an input convention, not a mechanism. The convention itself is what §15.41.3 r4 fixes ('an integer representation of offset from UTC expressed in minutes', re-checked), and r25 cases 3 and 4 pin it in BOTH directions on the UTC branch; combined with the single expression 'offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' that is a sound two-step reading, which is why the verdict survives. (4) THE CONSUME ARM WAS RE-READ CHARACTER BY CHARACTER, not inferred: in Analyze line 514 the test is 'if (c is not ('+' or '-'))', so both signs take the SAME skipped body and then the same pos++/continue -- there is no second arm to get wrong. I also measured the corpus: grepping every .cob under tests/conformance for an offset format shows NOTHING anywhere feeds a '-' or a '0' sign, or an extended '+hh:mm' subformat, into INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE / SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME / TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME (pb23 uses '+hhmm' with '+0500' only), so the row stays test-needed on the consume half.
